name: shelter
_note: out of the wind: 3 °C warmer on the beach, and you can sleep there without a fire
hint: A lean-to of logs against the rocks. Warmer, and you can sleep without a fire.

log: You lean the logs against the rocks and pack the gaps with sand and wrack.
Log by log, a lean-to rises against the rocks. You pack the gaps with wet sand.
You wedge the logs into the rocks, one beside the other, until the wind can't get in.

name: bed
hint: A frame of logs with a mattress of branches. You sleep deeper in it.

build.label: make
log: You lash two logs into a frame and heap it with springy branches.
A frame of logs, a deep layer of branches on top. It creaks when you test it.
Two logs, a mattress of branches. Not soft, but off the cold sand.

name: drying rack
hint: Fish hung in the wind and the smoke dry in 12 hours, and keep.

log: You drive two logs into the sand by the fire and lay a third across them.
Two uprights, a crossbar: a rack beside the fire, where the smoke drifts.
You build a rack of logs downwind of the fire.

start.label: hang fish
log: You split two fish and hang them over the crossbar.
Two fish, gutted and split, hang from the rack.
You hang the fish where the smoke can reach them.

collect.label: take down
log: The fish come off the rack stiff and dark.
Dry, hard, smelling of smoke. They will keep.
You take down the fish, dry as bark.

readyLog: The fish on the rack are dry.
The fish on the rack have dried.

name: rain barrel
hint: A hollowed log under the shelter's edge. It fills with rain in 12 hours.

log: You hollow a log with the axe and set it under the edge of the shelter.
Hour by hour the axe hollows the log. You stand it where the rain runs off.
A hollow log, set on end where the shelter drips.

start.label: set out
log: You tip the barrel upright under the edge of the shelter.
You set the barrel where the rain will run into it.

collect.label: drink
log: Rainwater, soft and cold. You drink your fill.
You drink from the barrel. It tastes of wood and sky.
Sweet rainwater, as much as you want.

name: fish trap
_note: anywhere you can fish: the shallows, the river. 1 fish every 2 hours, up to 3; stays set
hint: A woven willow trap: 1 fish every 2 hours, up to 3. It stays set.

log: You weave the willow into a long basket with a funnel at the mouth.
Twig over twig, the trap takes shape: a basket the fish can swim into and not out of.
You bend and weave the willow until you have a trap with a narrow mouth.

start.label: set
log: You weigh the trap down with stones, mouth to the current.
You sink the trap where the fish pass.
The trap goes in, weighted with a stone.

collect.label: empty
log: You haul the trap up, water streaming from the willow.
You lift the trap. Something heavy shifts inside.
Up comes the trap, dripping.

name: snares
hint: Rope nooses on the small trails. Check them after 12 hours.

build.label: make
log: You tie running nooses and peg them low over the trails.
Nooses of cord, pegged a hand above the ground where the trails narrow.
You knot the cord into snares and peg them along the runs.

start.label: set
log: You open the nooses and smooth the earth around them.
You set the snares and back away without a sound.
Each noose open, each peg firm. Now wait.

collect.label: check

text: A rabbit, cold and still in the noose.
One snare has caught: a rabbit.
A rabbit in the last snare.
Nothing. One noose has been pulled loose.
Nothing but tracks around the nooses.

log: You walk the trails from snare to snare.
You follow the runs, checking each noose.
One by one, you check the snares.

name: mushroom logs
hint: Oak logs soaked at the spring grow mushrooms in 2 days.

build.label: cut
log: You cut the oak into lengths and stack them in the shade, where the mushrooms grew.
The axe bites into the fallen oak. You stack the lengths in the damp shade.
Short oak logs, stacked in the shade beside the old trunk.

start.label: soak
start.requiresText: Needs water close by: the spring
log: You carry water from the spring and soak the logs dark.
Trip after trip from the spring, until the logs are soaked through.

collect.label: pick
log: Pale caps have pushed out of the bark. You pick them.
Mushrooms crowd the logs, soft and pale.
You twist the mushrooms off the bark.

cycle.readyLog: Mushrooms have come up on the logs.

name: corn field
hint: Corn sown here is ripe in 3 days.

build.label: dig
build.requiresText: Needs a hoe to break the ground
log: You break the ground with the hoe, row by row, and press the kernels in.
Hours of hacking at the turf. Then rows of dark earth, and the kernels pressed into them.
The hoe turns the soil over in long rows. You sow the corn and cover it.

start.label: sow
log: You hoe the rows again and sow them.
Kernels into the earth, one by one.
You sow the rows and cover them.

collect.label: harvest
log: You snap the ears off the stalks.
The stalks rustle as you break the ears off.
Ear after ear into your arms.

readyLog: The ears on the corn have filled out.

name: bee hive
hint: A hollow log for the wild bees. Honey every 3 days; smoke them first.

log: You hollow a log and stand it among the flowers, a hand-width hole near the top.
A hollow log, capped with bark, set on stones among the flowers.

start.label: lure bees
log: You smear crushed berries around the hole and wait.
Berry juice on the bark, to bring the bees.
You rub berries into the log's mouth. The humming comes closer.

collect.label: take honey
log: You smoke the bees drowsy and cut out a slab of comb.
Smoke, a slow hand, and a piece of dripping comb.
Under the smoke the bees go quiet. You take the comb.

name: fish weir
hint: A fence of stones and stakes across the river. Fish every 12 hours.

log: You wade in and build a wall of stones across the shallows, stakes between them, a gap at the end.
Stone by stone, a low wall grows across the river. You drive stakes into the gaps.
A fence of stones and stakes across the river, with one narrow way through.

start.label: close
log: You close the gap with a willow mat.
You block the weir's gap. The fish can come in, not out.

collect.label: empty
log: You wade into the pool behind the weir and catch the fish by hand.
Fish crowd the pool behind the stones. You scoop them out.
Behind the weir, the fish have nowhere to go.
